summary: The bill amends the Higher Education Act to bar accrediting agencies from denying recognition or accreditation based on an institution's racial, sex, or ethnic student/faculty composition or leadership and to require most agencies to verify that non-religious colleges protect free inquiry under the First Amendment or their own policies.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority. It solely amends accreditation criteria under the Higher Education Act.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses higher education accreditation only and has no connection to healthcare policy or coverage models.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, visas, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions concerning defense spending, military policy, or national security appropriations.
The bill makes no mention of environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.
No engagement with welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.

While the bill amends accreditation standards under the Higher Education Act, its focus is narrowly on free inquiry requirements and prohibitions on race/sex composition metrics rather than public school funding, federal involvement levels, school choice, or privatization. It does not align with the defined spectrum for this topic.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill contains no criminal justice reforms, sentencing provisions, or policing measures.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The legislation does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.

The bill prohibits accreditors from considering sex composition in certain contexts but does not expand or restrict legal protections specifically for LGBTQ+ individuals; any connection is indirect and incidental.
No provisions related to foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill does not address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No content concerning technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The legislation makes no reference to labor rights, union protections, or employer flexibility.

The bill explicitly exempts religious institutions (defined broadly to include those controlled by or committed to religious doctrines) from the new free inquiry accreditation requirements and allows them to maintain religious standards for faculty, students, and policies without penalty. This directly prioritizes religious exemptions over uniform application of other standards.
